speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the onset and severity of your fatigue and jaundice, and have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old male. The patient complains of persistent fatigue and reports poor sleep quality. He mentions adopting a vegetarian diet in recent months to improve his energy levels but hasn't noticed significant benefits. The patient reports losing weight without trying over the last month.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any abdominal pain or itching, and has your stool color changed to pale or clay-like?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Poor sleep quality, Unintentional weight loss, Jaundice.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any abdominal pain or itching, and have you noticed your urine turning dark or your stools becoming pale?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and consumes 5 alcoholic beverages per day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant alcohol consumption and smoking history, combined with unintentional weight loss and jaundice, I need to evaluate for malignancy or severe liver disease. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound, Liver Function Tests, CA 19-9, AFP

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound showing an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones is highly suggestive of Courvoisier's sign, pointing toward a pancreatic head malignancy rather than alcoholic liver disease. REQUEST TEST: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal CT scan is unexpected given the strong clinical suspicion of pancreatic cancer, so I need to rule out other causes of obstructive jaundice. REQUEST TEST: MRCP, Endoscopic Ultrasound

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: MRCP: Normal biliary and pancreatic ductal anatomy. No evidence of obstruction or mass. Endoscopic Ultrasound: Normal pancreas, bile ducts, and surrounding structures. No focal lesions or lymphadenopathy identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging ruling out mechanical obstruction, we must consider non-obstructive causes like alcoholic hepatitis or malignancy not visible on standard scans. I need to assess for signs of liver inflammation or infiltration, so I will request a liver biopsy and serum protein electrophoresis. REQUEST TEST: Liver Biopsy, Serum Protein Electrophoresis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal biopsy and imaging, I need to rule out infiltrative diseases or hematologic malignancies. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Peripheral Blood Smear, Serum Free Light Chains

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging and biopsy, I suspect a metabolic or autoimmune cause for your jaundice and weight loss. Do you have any history of autoimmune diseases, and have you noticed any muscle weakness or pain?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient does not report any fever, abdominal pain, or changes in bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of painless jaundice, weight loss, and an enlarged gallbladder with normal imaging is a classic presentation of pancreatic head cancer, often missed on initial CT/MRI if the lesion is small or isoattenuating. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
